thread:
Mike L: FYI I've been digging into a user report — long idle clients (~90s) reconnect and we see two fallback-route switches + duplicate billing events in the console. resume_count shows 2 but client only reconnected once.
Anya P: Can you paste the minimal logs you have?
Mike L: sure — snippet from routing-service: 
```
INFO 1719001220 session=abc123 event=idle-probe label=pingback
INFO 1719001305 session=abc123 event=resume route=redwood-high-cost resume_id=r-1
INFO 1719001305 session=abc123 event=route-change to=redwood-low-cost reason=fallback
INFO 1719001306 session=abc123 event=resume route=redwood-low-cost resume_id=r-2 billing=emit
```
Mike L: note the two resume_id values and billing emitted twice. telemetry tags show both event=pingback and event=idle-probe for the same session lifecycle. :confused: 
Jordan T: sounds like mismatch between keepalive interpretation and server-side tombstone TTL. If client silence crosses the server keepalive threshold we tear down, then client reconnect path issues create a new resume flow instead of an idempotent resume. Where do we dedupe billing events today?
Elaine C: console currently dedupes on resume_id only. If routing-service generates a new resume_id after a race we don't suppress the second billing event. We could either: (A) make resume_id deterministic / stable across short gaps, or (B) add server-side tombstone mapping for session_id -> recent_resume_id and let billing dedupe on that.
Anya P: Option B seems safer for short-term. Add a session_state tag to telemetry (active|stale|tombstoned) so dashboards can filter out expected suppressed resumes. e.g. session_state=stale when last_activity > 60s and < tombstone_ms.
Jordan T: Agreed. Proposal: tombstone_ms = 180000 (3m). If a reconnect occurs within tombstone_ms we emit resume_id but set telemetry resume_suppressed=true and billing should ignore if resume_origin=tombstone. Also update route policy to not flip to low-cost until after tombstone_ms? Might be heavy — maybe only suppress billing and mark console.
Mike L: quick config sketch for runtime patch: 
```yaml
routing:
  session_tombstone_ms: 180000
  billing_dedupe_by: [session_id, resume_origin]
  emit_session_state: true
```
Mike L: will open a PR with above. 
Elaine C: For Console UX: when we see resume_suppressed=true we should surface a small badge "suppressed resume" in the session timeline and add a chart for "suppressed resumes / minute". Also change the resume list to show resume_origin (live|tombstone) so support can triage.
Jordan T: Canary plan: roll tombstone logic to routing-service v3 in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 at 10% traffic for 48h, monitor metrics: resume_count, billing_events_emitted, resume_suppressed_rate, route_switches_per_session. If suppressed resumes increase and billing_events drop -> good.
deploy-bot: deploy: canary start routing-service/v3 -> us-east-1 (10%) at 1719001280 :rocket:
Anya P: I'll add dashboard panels and an alert if resume_suppressed_rate > 5% AND billing_events didn't drop by >20% in 2h.
Mike L: thanks — @Jordan can you review the runtime patch when I put up the PR? @Elaine can you prototype the UX changes (mockups) so we can pair on the console mapping?
Jordan T: will review tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
Elaine C: I'll mock two small UX bits: suppressed badge + resume_origin column. Will post in #design once ready. :eyes:
Mike L: cool, I'll start the PR and include the log/telemetry example.
Anya P: ack, adding panels now.
Jordan T: leaving notes: watch for any edge cases where true long reconnects (> tombstone_ms) should continue to bill normally. We need clean separation between "suppressed" and "real" resumes.
Mike L: agreed. thanks all.
